topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks open the lecture by introducing the topic of cancer therapy and outlining the expected learning outcomes.

topics.label: Conventional cancer treatments: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard therapeutic modalities that physically remove or broadly damage dividing cells, detailing their mechanisms of action, clinical successes, and limiting toxicities.

topics.label: Therapies exploiting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore treatment strategies designed to take advantage of specific tumor weaknesses, including hormone dependence, checkpoint defects, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss therapies directed against driving oncogenic kinases along with the structural, bypass, and adaptive mechanisms that cause clinical resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered antibodies are used to target cell-surface antigens, trigger immune clearance, and deliver targeted cytotoxic agents directly to tumor cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell redirection strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the relationship between the immune system and cancer, focusing on strategies that release immune checkpoints or genetically engineer T cells to attack tumor cells.

topics.label: Current challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer care
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the systemic challenges of heterogeneity and resistance, evaluate long-term trends in patient survival, and consider future scientific and ethical priorities in oncology.
